body.statement: Using \(H_{\mathrm{WF}}\), establish or refute universal constants \(c,C>0\) such that, without a dominance restriction, \[c\min\{1,\omega_\alpha(w,q)\}\le\mathcal R_\alpha(w,q)\le C\min\{1,\omega_\alpha(w,q)\},\qquad C^{-1}\omega_\alpha(w,q)\le\rho_\alpha(w,q)\le C\omega_\alpha(w,q).\] The proof must certify the explicit capped optimizer and its trimming dual, including all-measurable externally randomized intervals. When no cap binds, it must give \(\omega_\alpha=\sqrt{S\log(1/\alpha)}\).
body.justification: The capped optimizer and trimming dual are now proved; this question is retained solely for the matching all-measurable randomized-interval lower bound.
body.gap: A smooth-location weighted-erasure lower bound still needs moving-support endpoint control and a rigorous conversion from likelihood or Hellinger bounds to posterior interval spread.
body.consumer: Closing this question would turn the proved dominance-aware upper modulus into a two-sided minimax confidence-length frontier.

obligation.what_is_open: Prove the matching unrestricted minimax lower bound \(\mathcal R_\alpha\gtrsim\omega_\alpha\) for all measurable externally randomized intervals.
obligation.obstruction: The finite optimization and trimming duality are proved, but a capped perturbation by itself does not establish posterior interval spread under moving-support erasure laws.
obligation.attempted: The KKT optimizer, no-cap formula, trimming comparison, and minimax upper bound were closed. Per directive, the remaining route must separately prove the smooth-location erasure lower bound, endpoint control, and the likelihood or Hellinger-to-posterior-spread conversion.
obligation.partial_result:
The optimizer and trimming side are closed by \(\mathrm{lem{:}capped\text{-}trimming\text{-}duality}\):
\[
 \omega_\alpha\le\rho_\alpha\le4\omega_\alpha.
\]
Together with \(\mathrm{thm{:}trimmed\text{-}upper}\), this proves the unrestricted upper bound \(\mathcal R_\alpha\le8\omega_\alpha\).  If no cap binds, the active constraint gives \(\lambda_\alpha^2S=x_\alpha\) and hence \(\omega_\alpha=\lambda_\alpha S=\sqrt{Sx_\alpha}\).  The unproved part is the matching lower bound for all measurable externally randomized intervals; it requires the directed smooth-location erasure argument with explicit moving-support endpoint and posterior-spread control.
